title: MV RPG Maker MV Isometric Tileset s by LadyLuck

posts.author: JardsonJean
posts.body:
Hi, everyone! I have some assets I'm working on as a past time and I decided to share some of them here with you guys. I'm mainly looking for feedback and this is what I'd consider my first "pass". If you own RPG Maker MV, feel free to use and edit these in any way you want. If you end up using this in a project, just make sure to mention me somewhere or link to my page (Jardson Jean -
ladyluck.itch.io
). You can also reply to this thread with a screenshot, that way I can have a better notion as to how these are being used in practice.
Download all assets from this set for FREE individually from this thread or go visit my page for an all-in-one, single download option. More will be added as I work through them.
This set was made with parallax mapping in mind, its not supposed to fit perfectly on the RPG Maker MV grid and its not using any plugins or AI. I rendered most assets in bigger resolution so designers can shrink and adapt them as they see fit.
I used a couple of diferent methods and tools to make this work, so if you find some inconsistency let me know and I'll try my best to fix it on further iterations. You'll find 4 direction variations of a couple of these here, but that's not always going to be the case -- it just takes a lot of work to do them all. There's added depth to some of these, but in most cases I just kept the flat textures intact and visible blocky corners from the pixel art. I like how it makes the renders look retro.
Visible seams between the parts on the top part are expected when you line them up, but they're minor. You can clean it up using your prefered tool when creating maps.
TIPS FOR USE:
You can mix and match some of the top-down assets with the isometric ones. Even though they're not correctly lined with the enviroment, they still fit with the perspective.
You can also mix and match whatever parts work together like you would using the regular RTP.
If you need, for example, bigger/smaller tables, you can combine two renders and mask out parts of each separate render.
If you like these, consider visiting my itch.io page and share it around. Have fun!
ladyluck.itch.io
